utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'd like to deal with a few procedural matters to start with. First of all, if I have been unclear as far as the time is concerned still available for submissions in relation to Witness 7, you may interpret it in your own favour, three or four days. Then it was announced yesterday that the Defence would give an oral response on the videolink motion of the 21st of June, 2007, in relation to Witness 56. Could I hear from the Defence. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. After examining the information received, it seems to be evident that this particular witness can at this point travel by air; however, there may be the need for a second opinion. Based on the fact that the doctor's indication is such that he could travel, we would suggest that he come and testify in person, unless of course a second opinion indicates that that's not the case and that it would be inadvisable for him to travel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that you are aware that whether you can travel or not is not the only thing that matters, but that's the reason --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do appreciate that, Your Honour, and it's really based upon that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's based on that. Mr. Harvey, would you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No, I have nothing to add to that. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you stand distant from him?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No. I stand by my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I take it that you take this same position. Then three Defence teams are opposing the videolink requested for Witness 56. At this point, Mr. Kearney, I think positions are clear. I would like not to engage in lengthy litigation on this matter. Then the next procedural issue, the witness who was subpoenaed for today and for which I'm not quite sure that it has ever been considered to have protective measures for him, apparently has not appeared. At least, Madam Registrar, has there been anyone this morning reporting himself as saying that he was subpoenaed to testify today in this court? No. Then it's put on the record that a witness subpoenaed for today has not appeared in court to testify. The Chamber will consider what to do under the present circumstances. Then the next procedural item, the 16th motion for trial-related protective measures. Is there any Defence response that could be given in open session or is it -- I think it was yesterday announced that you would take a similar position once the witness appears. So nothing else at this moment to report. I see Mr. Guy-Smith nodding yes, and Mr. Harvey as well. Then we have the 14th motion for trial-related protective measures, and I do not know whether we have to go into private session to hear the response from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Depending on the level of detail of response that Your Honour wishes, I think it can be dealt with, at least initially, in open session. So far as we are concerned, on behalf of Mr. Haradinaj, the same position is adopted as in respect of the first two of this batch of witnesses; namely, that the basis for the application does not rise to the standard for the granting of protective measures under the Tribunal's jurisprudence. So we oppose the granting of protective measures, don't we.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's clear, and same position taken by Mr. -- by you, Mr. Guy-Smith, and by you, Mr. Harvey. Yes, then that's on the record. I think it might be wise not to go into any further details at this moment, and the Chamber, of course, will again read the application, within the back of our minds the objections expressed by you, Mr. Emmerson, and then see whether there's any need to further explore reasons for protective measures when the witness has arrived. These were the -- yes. I have one decision to be delivered. These are the reasons for granting protective measures for Witness 8. The Chamber owes the parties an explanation of its summary decision of the 4th of April, 2007, transcript page 2492, to grant Witness 8 the protective measures of pseudonym and face and voice distortion. The grant of protective measures was pursuant to a Prosecution motion dated the 3rd of April, 2007. The Prosecution submitted on behalf of Witness 8 that he had fled his home in Kosovo due to persecution, was living in unsettled temporary conditions in a neighbouring country, and that he had not returned to Kosovo since, out of fear that he would be harmed by KLA supporters. In response, on the 5th of April, 2007, the Defence jointly submitted that the Chamber's test for a grant of protective measures had not been met in the case of Witness 8 and that the requested measures were thus not justified. The reason why the present explanation by the Chamber comes at this time, that is to say, belatedly, is that the Chamber was until recently deliberating on a related decision, also on Witness 8. The related decision was handed down on the 20th of June of this year, and concerned the question of whether the Chamber should ask Witness 8 to return to The Hague to complete his testimony. As you are aware, the Chamber decided against calling for Witness 8's return at this time. In the 20th of June decision, we said, among other things, and I quote: "Most importantly, the witness's demeanour in court indicated weak memory or mental confusion." The Chamber had begun to form this impression already before Witness 8 began testifying on the indictment allegations. You will recall that on the 4th of April, 2007, Witness 8 was examined at some length by the Bench and the Defence about the requested protective measures before he began his testimony proper, I refer to transcript pages 2483 up to 2491. In the final analysis, when we delivered our summary decision, we were not confident that Witness 8 had sufficient awareness of his own safety and security situation to make a proper assessment of it for himself. Alternatively, even assuming that Witness 8 did have such awareness, the Chamber was not confident that he was sufficiently lucid or articulate to describe his personal situation with the accuracy necessary for the Chamber to decide a motion for protective measures. You will recall, for instance, that Witness 8, on the one hand, asked the Prosecution for protective measures; but, on the other hand, when in court said that he did not need the protective measures, transcript pages 2490 and 2491. In its discretion, the Chamber granted protective measures for Witness 8 exceptionally, out of an abundance of caution. This concludes the Chamber's reasons for granting protective measures for Witness 8. From what I remember, Mr. Kearney, for the reservations in relation to the admissibility of Defence Exhibits 56, 58, and 59, we need Mr. Re. Is that -- then it's not urgent. We'll leave it for the time being, and perhaps you can ask Mr. Re, when he's in court, to draw our attention to the fact that he's ready to explain those reservations. Then I think we could call the witness in for the continuation of the cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one brief matter. The Trial Chamber mentioned the fact that there was a subpoena issued for today with no appearance by the witness. Our records indicate that there was three such subpoenas for this week, and I just wanted to give the numbers to the Trial Chambers at this time of those witnesses. Was the Court referring to one particular witness or was it a broader statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think there was only one subpoena for today, but perhaps you check.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I will check our records. Our tentative review indicates that witnesses 10, 48, and 30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I must say, numbers are --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I know the name, but I'll not mention the name. I'll check which one it is, and perhaps it will be checked by Legal Officer whether it's 10, 48, or 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Tomas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony yesterday. Mr. Emmerson will now continue his cross-examination. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, I'm going to read you some passages from the evidence that you gave yesterday and then ask you some questions about it. On transcript page 6159, line 15, you said this, and you were referring to the 8th of September, you said: "Up until that moment, the Serb authorities had no opportunity or ability to come to that location. That was the first time we entered the territory as far as I am aware." You then said on the same page, line 21: "Since I was there in the field, I was naturally interested in going further away than Djakovica; however, that was strictly forbidden to us because that area was occupied by the terrorists or, to be more precise, that part of the territory was under the control of the terrorists. Therefore, there was absolutely no possibility of visiting that area." On 6160, line 6, you said this: "It is my position that this was the first entry of our forces into that part of the territory." And on the same page, at line 13 you, said this: "When referring to that part of the territory, I am referring to the area to the right of the Djakovica-Peje road and to the left of the Djakovica-Peje road." Do you stand by that evidence?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by my evidence, and especially given the fact that, as far as I know, none of us who had come from elsewhere to assist our colleagues was able to move anywhere else, except on the main road towards Pec and the other one towards Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, there were Serb forces stationed in the area of Lake Radoniq from the moment you arrived until the 8th of September, were there not?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb forces were not stationed at Lake Radonjic. As far as I know, the Serb forces did not arrive until after we had visited Lake Radonjic. I know that on the basis of the fact that once we notified that we had arrived in the area, the uniformed people came to secure the area so that they could exhume the bodies that were found at Lake Radonjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There were Serb forces stationed not only at the lake itself, but also on a hill on the western side of the lake known as Suka Bitesh or Suka Radoniq, I suggest --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object, that's a compound question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, it's not, he's answered the first proposition by denying that there were Serb forces at the lake. I'm saying that in addition to that there were Serb forces stationed on Suka Bitesh or Suka Radoniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, if that's at case, with all respect to my colleague, this witness denied Serb forces being at the lake so therefore it's an improper question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I take Your Honour's point. It's a phraseology issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, there were Serb forces in addition stationed on a elevated position to the west of the lake, Suka Radoniq, sometimes called Suka Bitesh, I suggest?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I have to reply, I will say that I'm not aware of that. All I know is that when we arrived at Lake Radonjic, that was the first entry of our forces into the area of Lake Radonjic. That's what we were told. You were able to see in this statement given by persons that we interviewed that the area around Lake Radonjic was under the control of the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which route did you take to reach the lake, Mr. Tomas? From Djakovica which route did you take on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, given that I was quite new to the area and I wasn't familiar with the terrain, we travelled on the main road. We reached a place on the road between Djakovica and Pec. We stopped there because we were travelling in a convoy of several cars. There were people securing us and the entire mission. We left our vehicles, and then we continued on foot. I can't tell you exactly through which settlements we passed because I was not familiar with the area. I just followed the people who were our guides.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know of a village called Prilep?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it's an intersection, or rather, it's a settlement at the intersection on the road from Djakovica to Prizren. And as far as I remember, it's located on the right from the road. I remembered this location because there were a lot of individual attacks, be it against civilians or members of security forces travelling on that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you pass Prilep on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, I didn't know at the time the settlements through which we travelled because I had been there only several months prior to that and that was the first time I left Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, when you earlier said that Prilep was on the right of the road from Djakovica to Prizren, is that what you meant to say or ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I was able to see afterwards, since I remained there for some time after that and travelled to Pec several times, I realised that Prilep was located on the right of the road Djakovica-Pec.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On the 8th did you happen to see a contingent of approximately 300 Serb forces, combined police and VJ forces, razing Prilep to the ground or razing any of the villages in that area to the ground?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that right now. That wasn't my line of thinking at the time. At the time all I was interested in was reaching Lake Radonjic as soon as possible. So I cannot comment on what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see Serb forces setting fire to people's houses that day?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have occasion to see that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Let me come back to your answer then, please, that the Serb forces were unable to penetrate at all the territory on either side of the main road. Could you turn in the bundle, please, to tab 14. This is a witness statement from (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we look at paragraph 10 of that witness statement, we can see the dates upon which your immediate superior was posted to Djakovica, that is, the 1st of July, 1998, until the 1st of October or November, 1998. And with that information in mind, could you please turn to paragraph 18 of the witness statement. I'm going to read this into the record, if I may. "The public police (MUP) in cooperation with our operatives seized documents from KLA of precise information on who smuggled weapons. I cannot remember exactly which house they entered first because they entered several houses and seized documentation. This was done regularly throughout the period of time. I was there starting from July 1998." He then goes on to describe the types of documentation that were seized and then continues four lines -- five lines further down. "This usually came about when either the MUP or the RDB received information about KLA staff in the village and we would conduct an operation aimed at seizing weapons and arresting perpetrators. This documentation was seized from villages such as Smonica, Jablanica" -- you know those two villages, Mr. Tomas?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard of Jablanica, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On the western side of the main road. "Rastavica, Babaloc, Dujak, Skivjan" on the eastern side of the main road, "Reka Kec," on the west side of the main road, "Gllogjan and Rznic. In the same way, the RDB also obtained lists with data on KLA members who were involved in terrorist activities." Now pausing there. Your superior had made a statement, which he signed very recently, indicating that RDB operatives working with the MUP regularly conducted raids on both sides of the main road throughout the time he was is there from July to November 1998. I'd like to ask you, please, to commented on how that is being capable of being reconciled with the evidence that you have given to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the form of the question. I believe --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll put it another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: If I can complete my objection. I believe it mischaracterises the statement of (redacted). Later on, in his testimony, he talks about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you would not read that for the time being, but refer us to the paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This same paragraph where it talks about these seizures being made only when operations were conducted aimed at seizing weapons and perpetrators. This is different than free access on both sides of the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, free access has not been the language. Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll put the question in a different way, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've seen that passage, Mr. Tomas, you told us, on oath yesterday, that the 8th of September was the very first time any Serb forces entered any territory on either side of the main Peje to Gjakove road. That was a lie, the evidence you gave yesterday, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that it was the first time I went out on the field. It was my impression, and we were told, that up until that time our forces had had no access to Lake Radonjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, that's not the answer that you gave on oath, Mr. Tomas. The answer you gave on oath was that it was your position that the 8th of September was the first entry of our forces into that part of the territory, which you explained meant the area to the right of the Peje to Gjakove road and the area to the left. And when you gave that evidence yesterday, you knew it was a lie, didn't you, Mr. Tomas?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't lie yesterday. I said that, as far as I know and as far as I was told, that was the case. That was the first time we went out in the field, and we were told that up until that time our forces had had no access to that area. If I may continue. Had they had access, then logically they would have come across what we came across on that day. But given that a large number of civilians, both Serbs and Albanians, were kidnapped, their fate was not known up until that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is it your evidence, Mr. Tomas, that the person who made this witness statement never told you of these regular RDB operations, even though you were there working in the same building with him over this period of time?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who gave this statement was an officer in charge of the department where I worked. This person was quite in a different position in relation to me because all information ended on his desk. So it was quite different. I spoke of specific tasks. As for other information, I had no access to it. He received it from other operatives. And in that sense, he was much better informed than I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, you do not have to explain happened, as you said, what happened. You do not have to explain to us whether there's any logic in it. You just have to tell us - and the question was quite simple - did he ever tell you. And I do now understand that your answer is no. And whether he could have known what he could have told you is not something we should speculate on at this moment. So please focus very much on the precise question put to you and then answer that question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, we have viewed in this courtroom a videotape of Serb forces, including paramilitary police forces, entering and taking control of Gllogjan and Irzniq on the 11th of August. We've heard evidence of major Serbian offensives in the area to the east of the main road in the second half of May, in the second half of July, and well into August. We've seen documents recording Serbian offensives on the western side of the main road in May and beyond. Are you telling the Trial Chamber that you were entirely unaware of the fact that Serb forces penetrated the areas either side of the main road during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to remind you that I arrived there in late July. The period that you are referring to could apply to the first days of my stay there. I wasn't in the position to know what was happening during the initial stage of my stay in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, again, I have to address you. The question was whether you were aware. Of course, it's quite clear, you clearly have given testimony when you arrived. But to say, "Then I'm not in a position," either you are aware or you are not aware, and there are many ways in which you can obtain awareness. I sometimes have awareness of matters I've never seen myself happening somewhere else. I even have awareness of events that took place before I was born. No reasoning, please, no logic, just answer the question. If you were aware, perhaps the next question of Mr. Emmerson might be: How did you become aware? And if your answer is: I was not aware, then we'll see what next question will be. So please focus on the questions and answer them to start with. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is your evidence, Mr. Tomas, just so we're clear, that although the person who made the witness statement we just looked at was aware of the raids that took place after he arrived in July, until the moment you walked into this witness box yesterday, it was your honest belief that there had been no Serb forces either side of the main road. Is that your position? That was your honest belief until you walked into the witness box yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object. Vague as to time. There have been no forces -- no Serb forces on either side of the main road during what time-period?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At any time prior to the 8th of September, which was the witness's testimony on oath yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Is this only in 1998? Is it other time-periods? It's a very vague question in terms of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's perfectly obvious, with the greatest respect, what the question is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can ask -- Mr. Kearney, you can ask what has happened before a certain moment in time, and then from the answer we'll find out whether we need further precision. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just finally on this topic, Mr. Tomas, you told us unequivocally yesterday, on more than one occasion, and your exact words just to assist Mr. Kearney were these: "Up until that moment, the Serb authorities had no opportunity or ability to come to that location." And you said later on: "It is my position that this was the first entry of our forces into that part of the territory." The question I was asking you was: When you came into the witness box yesterday, was that your genuine belief?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my belief at the time, and it is still my belief to this day, that that was the case. That's the information that I had at my disposal, and this is what I believed, given that we were told that we were unable to go either to the right or to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So my question to you is: Who told you - never mind what you were able to do as an individual - who told you at the time in 1998 that there were no Serb operations penetrating into those two areas of territory and no Serb forces in those areas? Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I was assigned, along with others, we came from elsewhere and we were told by our superior officers not to wander off the road, not to go anywhere off the road. That's what our superior officers told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that was the basis of your evidence yesterday, that there were no Serb forces in the area, that you yourself had received instructions not to wander off the main road. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever I did there was the result of the tasks given to me. Of course, it had to do with our safety. On the other hand, I personally never heard of any of our lot being able to penetrate, either to the left or to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please, to turn to the witness statement that you've made. I'm turning to another topic now. You'll find your witness statement that you signed and that referred to in your testimony yesterday, dated the 23rd of May, 2007, behind tab 1 in that yellow file. Perhaps you can turn it up, please, and find your way to paragraph 22. The Serbian is behind the tab. I'm going to ask you some questions now about the process of interview of Ljulj Musaj and Zenelj Alija. Before we go through those paragraphs, Mr. Tomas, can I just ask you one question which doesn't require reference to your statement. When you left the canal on the 8th of September, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 8th of September, we were at Lake Radonjic. That evening I went back with my chief, the chief of the secretariat, and the driver. That was sometime between dusk and night-time. I know that we arrived in Djakovica later on and that we were being -- and it was raining, and the driver was familiar with the general area. This means that the driver was a local person.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please do try and follow the Judge's request, to answer the question I'm asking you directly and shortly. You've told us that when you left the canal you went to Djakovica. Where in Djakovica did you go? Did you go back to the police station or did you go to your home?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to the secretariat first, I believe, the secretariat meaning the place where we worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Pause there. Did you go back to work that evening or did you go home after going into the secretariat?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had an office there. Of course, I must have stayed there for a while. I can't remember how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. And finally this: Do you remember what you were doing back at Djakovica police station that evening?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We must have first sorted out our impressions of the day and put some sort of an information brief together.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: About the visit to the canal?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what else we could have done that evening after such a taxing day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure that we all understand that, Mr. Tomas. Let's move on. Paragraph 22 of your witness statement, I just want to ask you about paragraph 22, paragraph 23, and paragraph 29, and make sure I've understood your testimony correctly. In paragraph 22 in the second sentence, when you are referring to the interviews with Mr. Musaj and Mr. Alija, you say this: "The initial interviews took place on the 7th September, 1998. My (late) colleague, Dejan Jovovic and I interviewed two KLA members who had been arrested and brought to us by the MUP Djakovica." And in paragraph 23, you say this: "The names of the two KLA members were Zenelj Alija and Ljulj Musaj who were arrested by the MUP." A little further down in that paragraph, you say: "We carried out the interview in our office. We only spoke to them for one day. We did not mistreat them or harm them in any way." Now, pausing there for a moment, is it true that you only spoke to them for one day, as you say there in your witness statement. Is that the truth, Mr. Tomas?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked to them on the 7th, then we received the first information of interest to us; namely, the execution site at Lake Radonjic, including the information provided by Zenelj concerning the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, please, don't repeat the information, just answer the question. The question I'm asking you is whether -- you've told us you talked to them on the 7th, and that was the first time you received the information about Lake Radonjic. The question I'm asking you is: Is it true, as you say there, in your signed witness statement that you told us yesterday was correct, is it true that where you say: "We only spoke to them for one day." Is that true? Yes or no will do, Mr. Tomas.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't. It's not true that we spoke to them only one day. We had interviews with them in the subsequent days, too, on the matters of interest to us. We used the opportunity provided by the law to speak to them for three days; that's to say, 72 hours. That was the time-period granted to us by the law, and we spoke to them, therefore, on the 7th and the 9th and the 10th. I'm not sure about the time-line, though. We were supposed to take statements from them and supplement some of the information we already had. What I want to say is that it wasn't just for one day that we talked to them. We started our interview of them on the 7th and ended it on the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Why did you write that in your witness statement and sign it then: "We only spoke to them for one day." If it wasn't true, why did you sign that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm going to object to the form of that question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- Members of the Trial Chamber. There has been no allegation that that statement is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I wonder if the witness can take his headphones off while we have this discussion perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take your earphones off for a while, Mr. Tomas. Mr. Emmerson, it's my recollection that the Prosecution took two witness -- also two later statements taken. He was talking about dispatches, I think, that were --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those are not, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- not contained in the first and then later on statements were given. We have the unsure date of the 10th of September there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So to put to the witness where he testified about these matters that, "We only spoke to them for one day," that could mean a lot of things, like we only spoke to them before we entered -- I would like to have that put in context, because it is, at least in my recollection, it's clear that the witness never in his testimony gave the impression that after that one day there was no further interviews anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be absolutely clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The witness's evidence was that there were records compiled days after the interview took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I am commenting on each of those records, and I can take Your Honours after the break to the transcript references. The witness commented that the records --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then try top clarify that, whether there were any -- at least, it's not my recollection that he said -- well, that was the only day. I do agree that he was talking about follow-up, and I think it would be -- would better assist the Chamber if we would try to clarify that, whether there was any further interviews, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed, once the witness has put his earphones on again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How many times after the 7th did you personally take part in an interview of Zenelj Alija?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to try and remember. I know that we spoke to him on the first day. We spoke to both of them separately on that first day. I think we had our interview of them on two or three occasions, because we were supposed to make a separate note on the formation of their terrorist group, that constituted one note and one statement on that matter; and the other statement would have been a supplement on the Ratis issue, as we refer to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Can I ask you, please, in that context of that answer to explain what you meant in the witness statement where you are recorded and have signed to say: "We only spoke to them for one day." What did you mean by that sentence, please?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I wanted to say was that after this interview, which took place over only one day, we received information that were priority to us. On the 7th, we received all the information that was a matter of priority to us, and that's why I put it that way. After this one-day interview, we received all the information that were important -- that was important to us. That's why it was entered this way in my statement, probably, because it was on the priority matters that we received all the information needed after that one day of interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Pause there for a moment. I'm going to suggest to you that Zenelj Alija was arrested in the area of Kodralija on the 3rd of September, that is, a full four days before you say you went to the canal and three days before you say you interviewed him; and that he was detained in Djakovica police station during that period of time, where he was beaten. Can I ask you to respond to that, please, that he'd been detained in the police station since the 3rd of September and was being beaten during that time?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when Zenelj Alija was brought in. The only thing I know was that he was brought to me only the 7th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And I'm going to suggest to you that Ljulj Musaj was arrested on the 5th of September and was beaten whilst in police custody. I ask you to respond to that, please.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, too, is not known to me. I don't know about that. I was telling you that these were persons brought over to us for an interview. I don't know how they were treated or when they are elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. You say "elsewhere," the MUP shared the same building with you, did they not?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we were on the top-most floor; whereas, all the other premises belonged to MUP. We were basically under the same roof, but were part of different organisational units.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll come to that -- the flaws of the building in a little while. You were on the top floor and the prisoners were kept in the basement. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you turn behind tab 9, please. This is a documented complaint recorded on the 9th of November, 1999, by the human rights organisation in Kosovo concerning Ljulj Musaj. And you may not -- I think, it may be that the version you have contains an Albanian original in manuscript. We have a typescript in English. Do you read Albanian? Do you read Albanian, Mr. Tomas?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me read to you the substance of the complaint, and this is page 1, item 1. The date of the alleged crime is given as the 5th of September and the perpetrator is a man called Rade Vlahovic, and Mr. Musaj lodged a complaint that reads as follows: He was beaten for ten days in a row. "Ljulj Musaj, 32 years old, from Ratishe i Ulet on the 5th of September, 1998, in the village of Trakaniq, I was there with two persons," and he gives their names, "both from the village of Novo Sello and Dukagjin, and we were going to the house of" another person he names. And then he says this: " Unexpectedly, we were stopped by the police. Three police officers, who, after identifying us and checking the whole vehicle, called for other forces and took me to the police station in Djakovica -- Gjakove." "After they took me to the police station in Gjakove, they immediately started beating me; and after a while, the police inspector, Rade Vlahovic, from Ratishe i Eperm in municipality of Decan, interrogated me. While interrogating me, this police officer has beaten in the most brutal way. While interrogating me, he told me on several occasions: Are you married? How many children do you have? "After I told him that I have two children, he told me that after two days they will bring my children there and cut off their heads in front of you. While we will send" you "to the Albanian border, put some weapons next to" you "and execute" you. In the police station, they kept me for ten days, and on the 14th they released me."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, before you continue, it's only now --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that the transcription could be finished. Please, when reading, next time, slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know who Rade Vlahovic is, Mr. Tomas, or was at the time?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He most certainly was not a member of the state security structure. He could only have been a member of public security. On the other hand, what you've just read out to me is something I was not aware of, that something of the sort was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, again, no one asked you at this moment whether you are aware of anything that was read to you. The simple question was whether you knew Mr. Vlahovic. Would you please focus your answers on the questions put to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So can I repeat the question: Do you know Rade Vlahovic, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might have seen him or could have been seeing him at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let's be clear, because there's some ambiguity in that answer, Mr. Tomas. In September 1998, did you know who Rade Vlahovic was?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that I knew the man personally in September. As I said, I stayed there for a short period of time and I would only come across people and know them by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Could you just turn behind tab 15 for a moment, please. There's a witness statement there of a man whose name I won't mention, but who was a senior member of the SUP working from the Djakovica police station; and if you could just find paragraph 30 in the Serbian, where dealing with the interviews of a number of men, including Zenelj Alija, this witness says as follows: "The interviews of these terrorists were led by the crime in respecters of SUP Djakovica. I recall Radovan Zlatkovic, Dusan Dragovic, Rade Vlahovic, and Ljubisa Novavic being involved in these interviews. I also remember that interviews were also conducted by the state security police officers, but I don't remember their names." So it would appear, Mr. Tomas, as that Rade Vlahovic was taking part in the process of interviewing men, including Zenelj Alija. Did you not know that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that. This is the first time seeing that, that an earlier interview was taken of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. We'll come to whether it was the first time that you knew that, Mr. Tomas, in just a little while. But can I ask you: Who handed them over to you, then? What were the names of the officers who handed them over to you, these two men?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Can you look briefly behind tab 10, because this is a statement that Mr. Musaj has made in connection with these proceedings, where he describes what happened to him in a little more detail. And, again, it may -- I think this does not have a Serbian translation, so I'm going to have to read this to you into the record, and I'll do it at an appropriate speed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The appropriate speed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm alive to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "It was sometime in the afternoon when we arrived at the police station."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Counsel, I'm sorry. Where are you reading in this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry. Page 3 just below halfway. I will repeat what I've read.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "It was sometime in the afternoon when we arrived at the police station."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting my colleague again. This appears to be a question along the same lines of what Mr. Musaj said happened to him before he had contact with this witness. This witness has already said he was not aware of a beating or a prior interview. I fail to see the relevance of reading yet another quotation from another document to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it will become apparent because of the detail of what is being put by this witness in this statement and by the following witness in the following statement. If there's a specific objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, yes, I didn't know whether it was a specific objection or whether it's just an observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The objection was relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For a third time then: "After a short while" -- I'm sorry. "It was sometime in the afternoon when we arrived at the police station. In the police station, I saw one police officer which I recognised. His name was Rada Vlahovic. We knew each other very well as a child. Rada was from the village Upper Ratishe, and we were going to the same school. "When Rada saw me at the police station, he started to beat me immediately. Rada didn't ask anything of me. He was beating me until one of the police officers came and stopped him. I didn't know that police officer, but I saw that he was high-ranking senior officer in uniform. He ordered Rada to take me to his office. "Rada took me to his office which was, I think, was on the second or the third floor of the police station. "When we got to the office, there were two police officers already in there. They were dressed in civilian clothes. This included Rada Vlahovic, who took me there. "In the office, Rada showed me several broomsticks and asked me with which one I would like to be beaten with. "All of them in the office beat me for several hours until I fainted. All this happened on the same day, the 5th September, the day that I was arrested. "They didn't interview me on the first day, they just beat me. When they had finished with me, Rada and two other officers took me back downstairs and put me in the basement of the police station." Then a little bit further down, he says: "The next day they took me from the basement and brought me again to the office. I don't remember if it was the same office, but I know that there were the same officers present; Rada and the other two civilians. "In the office, they started swearing at me and began to beat me. Rada said to me that I had killed his mother and his father."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "And for that reason, he was going to kill all the children." Now, if you could just look over to the following page, page 5, two-thirds of the way down, the last-but-one paragraph. "On the third day, again, I was taken to the office in the police station. This time it was in a different office and by different officers. They beat me and asked me if I knew who were the organisers of the KLA soldiers in the village and the names of the KLA who were going to Albania." And he then goes on to describe being taken to the canal, where he en route was made to lie on the floor of the vehicle. Now, pausing there for a moment, the third day of course he's referring to there, where he's taken to different police officers or different officers who by the way him, that would be the 7th, wouldn't it, the day of the interview you claim to have conducted? Wouldn't it, Mr. Tomas?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To say that I interviewed him is not quite appropriate in my mind because I don't speak Albanian. I was present at the interview with a colleague of mine, but he wasn't mistreated at the time at all. This is the only thing I can state, that he was not mistreated when we were there at all. I came from a centre where such measures are unacceptable. Throughout my career at the centre, I was trained not to resort to the use of force in my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you some questions about that in a moment or two, Mr. Tomas. But just so that we're clear about this, Rade Vlahovic was the son of a couple called Milko and Miloica Vlahovic, who believed that his parents had been killed by the KLA and their bodies disposed of in the canal. And I want to ask you this: Did you know that one of the police officers who'd interviewed these men was the son of someone who he believed to have been killed by the KLA and dumped in the canal? Were you aware of the fact that one of the interviewing officers was a relative of someone believed to be a victim?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that question misstates this witness's testimony. He said that he didn't know that these individuals were interviewed by anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see. Well, we'll come to that in a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it then you withdraw the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll put the question in a different form.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware that one of the officers who had dealt with the two men that you had interviewed had a relative or had relatives who he believed to have been killed by the KLA and dumped in the canal?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that because I was quite new to the area. I had only been there for a month at that point. I didn't know any of those stories.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Whilst we're on this part of the evidence, could you turn to tab 11. This is a witness statement made by Zenelj Alija, which makes similar allegations. I'm looking on page 3. I'll read it to you in English, so you get Serbian translation. This is at the top of page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, could you start at low speed and finish at low speed as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "I was kept in a basement of the police building on my own. It was dark and the door was guarded. I was kept in this state for a total of 12 days. The only time that I left the room was to be taken to another part of the building where I was spoken to by the police. "The rooms that I was taken to changed all the time, but I remember that it was always on either the fourth or the fifth floor of the station. "I was interviewed in these rooms. The police there would beat me with batons; and, on some occasions, I was also tortured with electric shocks. I do not know what they were saying to me because they always spoke in Serbian language. "I frequently passed out, but this did not stop them from continuing to beat me when I regained consciousness. "I was forced to sign a document during this time. I did not know what it said because I was never shown it to read. It could not be a true document because I did not say anything to the police." He then goes on to describe being taken to the canal, being made to lie face-down on the floor of the vehicle, and saying that the police officers in the back of the vehicle sat with their feet on his back. Now, pausing there for a moment. Just to be clear, your office, was it on the fourth or the fifth floor?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was on the fifth. It's the last floor of the building. That's where our office was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would suggest to you again, Mr. Tomas, that these men were beaten whilst in custody.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: While they were in our office, these people were not beaten, and I explained to you the reasons for that; my presence and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll ask you a little bit more about that, Mr. Tomas. I assume from the answer you've given us, you say that you personally have never used physical force during an interrogation of a suspect. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And have you ever witnessed another member of the RDB using physical force during an interrogation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Objection as to relevance for these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Indiscernible] --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: He's been a career officer for two and a half decades.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's a credibility question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Have you ever witnessed another member of the RDB use physical force during an interrogation, yes or no, Mr. Tomas?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in my presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Have you ever learned of RDB members using physical force during interrogations?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never talked to anyone about those issues. We had enough work. We had to work. We couldn't just sit around and chat on such topics.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And when suspected KLA members were brought into the secretariat in Gjakove, were you never aware of them being beaten either by RDB officers or by officers of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know when the members of RDB could have had the occasion to beat him. As far as I know, members of the RDB never participated in operations where people were arrested, especially since numbers of our personnel were such that we were unable to participate in such operations. Given the amount of people we had, it was hard enough for us to handle the interviews of the people who had been arrested by MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to look, if I may, with you against that background, please, about some of the documents that Mr. Kearney took you to yesterday and I want to start, please, with -- behind tab 2. This is, for the record, Exhibit P373. If you could just turn behind tab 2 in the yellow file, please. First of all, this is a document you told us yesterday and the original is dated the 10th of September, and you said it was a description of the information provided by Ljulj Musaj in the interview that you had conducted with him on the 7th. And you said you wrote it up at some days after, a couple of days I think was your specific testimony. Can you just help us, about five lines down from the top, just above the entry that has a number 2 on it, are four lines which describe when the interview was conducted. And it records there that the interview was conducted between the 8th and the 9th in the offices of ORDB Djakovica. Now, you wrote this document, you tell us, on the 10th. Why was it that you made no reference to the interview that you say took place on the 7th?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please turn to page 4 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the last paragraph, where it says: The Prizren CRDB was duly informed of the statements made in the note by dispatches number 562 dated 7th of September, 1998, it's precisely what I said, that on the 7th, when we gained first information, we informed the centre in the quickest possible way by sending a dispatch. So the interview that was conducted on the 7th was transformed into a dispatch and sent, as indicated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, you know those dispatches have been destroyed, don't you, the original documents have all been destroyed. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no way for me to know that. I didn't know that. Nobody has every told me that before and there was no way for me to learn that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we can turn up the relevant passage of the statement of an individual who worked with you in relation to the those records later on, but for the time being if you can take it from me that the original dispatches have all been destroyed. The question I'm asking you in relation to this document is why it would be on the 10th that you would record that the interview took place on the 8th and the 9th if it had taken place on the 7th and you had, in fact, been at the lake on the 8th? What is the explanation for that, please?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember right now, nor do I have an explanation. Whether we made a mistake with the date, I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well, we'll look at some other documents in a moment, but if you look at page 2 just for a second for your own use. If you could just look about two-thirds of the way down on page 2 in the Serbian, and this is the last full paragraph on page 2 in the English, can you see a paragraph that begins to make a description of the Bishtrica river and sets out certain information about the canal there. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just please tell me which paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Page 2, paragraph -- it's halfway down the fourth paragraph. You see a reference to the river Bishtrica and to Lake Radoniq --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you find 400 and 500, it's immediately --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you just familiarise yourself briefly with that passage, that contains a detailed description of the location of the canal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course, by the time you wrote this, as the document itself reveals, you yourself had already been there, hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when this was written - and this was written on the 10th - it's a shame that we don't have the dispatch of the 7th where you would be able to see that we had given the same description. In the dispatch on the 7th, we informed precisely of the execution site and Lake Radonjic. We made the description of this based on the information provided by the persons interviewed. The two of us who worked on this case - and I was from outside the area, as was the case with my colleague - none of us had visited Lake Radonjic previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Could you turn behind tab 3 for a moment, please, which is a witness statement signed by yourself and by Ljulj Musaj and, I think, by your colleague Mr. Jovovic. And if you just like to cast your eye, in the Serbian, to the first page four lines up from the bottom, and then following it on, can I ask you -- in the English translation, this is page 2 eight lines down from the top a sentence beginning: "I also know ..." Can I ask you, please, to confirm that the text in that document is identical to the text in the document you've just shown us from the 10th, or at least it's more or less identical. I don't want you to compare it word for word. It's the same information, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The official note on an interview conducted needs to be essentially consistent with the statement signed by the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just asking you to confirm that that is the position. I don't want to take a great deal of time on it because we can make the comparison for ourselves, Mr. Tomas. It is essentially, if you scan across it, the same information, is it not; and in many respects, the same language?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can just ask to have counsel clarify. Behind tab 3, we're talking about a sentence that begins with: "I also know ..." Is that correct, counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And then behind tab, we're talking about a sentence which begins with: "I will describe it:"?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, it begins at paragraph -- page 2, last full paragraph: "I also know ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, can I just ask you this, please, about this document. If you look in the very first line of it, very, very first line of the document, you see the opening lines at the top there. There's an introductory paragraph, and what date does it give for the interview there?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to the document under tab 2, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. I'm referring to the document, Mr. Tomas, behind tab 3. Behind tab 3, the document that you have in your right hand, there are four lines at the top, please, at the top of the page. Can you tell us what date it gives as the date for the interview?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here the 8th of September, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pause there, please. Now, you told us yesterday that sometimes documents are written up on a different day from the date that the interview takes place. So what I'm asking you, please, to tell us is whether the 8th of September is supposed to be the date that the interview took place or the date that this note was written up.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the date when the statement was written. Based on this document, that's the only explanation I can give; namely, that the statement was drawn up on the 8th.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And yet the document we looked at a moment ago also recorded the interview taking place on the 8th and the 9th and not the 7th; that is, the document behind tab 2. You agree with that? You told us that that was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the first interview was conducted on the 7th. Could we please differentiate. The day when an interview is conducted is one thing, and the day when a statement was drawn is another. It mentions both the 8th and the 9th here, and it's difficult for me to discern them right now. It's hard for me to say whether it's the 8th or the 9th because one date covers the other date, so it is not quite clear. But it seems to me that it could have been on the 9th that the statement was drawn up, looking at the document, because one date was typed over the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where --

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Logically --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which document are you looking at, please, where you said there's a date typed over another one. Where is that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the original fourth line gives a bit of an unclear 8, which may have been something else. It's not an unambiguous 8. That's what the witness refers to apparently. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I don't -- I can see the 8. It doesn't look unambiguous to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, at the left bottom side of the 8, there is some thing, and the opening you would usually find at the right-hand side between the upper and the lower circles of the 8 seems to be filled to some extent. So I understand, at least, what the witness is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If it's been changed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have an 8 and a 9 nearby for comparison.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If it's been changed, Mr. Tomas, from a 9 to an 8, that would be by either yourself or Mr. Jovovic to correct it, would it not? It's been corrected into an 8, if anything at all?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're asking me about something that happened nine years ago. It seems that the date is clearly corrected here. There's another matter here. It is quite possible that this mistake was caused by the fact that people were not quite sure about the date. So it's logical to assume that first they typed one date and then they corrected it. We worked day and night, and sometimes we were confused with the dates ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Certainly, if it was the 8th, can you help us, you were -- left the secretariat first thing in the morning and didn't return until after dusk?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could have -- could be 9th, too, because the date is typed over. I'm more inclined to believe that this is the 9th of September than the 8th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, would that be a convenient moment to break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it would be a convenient moment. We promised you, Mr. Emmerson, to give you some guidance at the end of the first session. Let me -- first of all, how much time you would have in mind that you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would have thought another hour and 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the Chamber would like you to try to do your utmost best to finish in one hour on return. And, for example, to ask the witness about a certain date or -- there are matters you asked the witness which could clearly be seen by everyone who looks at the document. I remember that -- let me just see. I am now wondering whether it was exactly this 8th or the 9th, but you seem to be not looking at the original you said. Well, I'll check that. There were some questions which --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm certainly happy to speed up. The documents take a little time and there are a picture to build it up. There are other documents and dates that one needs to look at. I'll do it as quickly as I can. I will certainly do it within in Your Honour's restrictions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break until 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, I want to take you as quickly as possible, please, through three further documents. Could you look, first of all, behind tab 4. This is a document that you were shown yesterday by Mr. Kearney, which is -- are you behind tab 4?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'd just like to ask you to confirm that on this document, which you wrote on the 16th of September detailing your dealings with Zenelj Alija, you recorded that the interview took place on the 9th and 10th of September. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the continuation of the interview conducted on the 9th and 10th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And that document records Mr. Alija allegedly having told you, both about the lake and about bodies found at Dashinoc. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was definitely for Dasinovac, and as for the lake, that he was familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we can turn behind tab 5 for a moment, you will find there a witness statement signed by Zenelj Alija which is, if you can help me with this, co-signed by two individuals; Zivojin Stankovic and Dusan Dragovic. Do you know who those two men are?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only suppose that, on the basis of the previous text and on the basis of the heading, that they were members of the public security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And I think we saw their names earlier on as being part of the group -- or at least one of them as being part of the group of officers from the MUP involved in this series of interviews. Now, if we look towards the top of the page, you can see that this memorandum is dated the 4th of September and refers in the first opening lines to the fact that Mr. Alija was brought in for questioning on the 3rd of September. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that in the heading the date is the 4th of September. This is when the document was created.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then if you look at --

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that it says here on the 3rd and then in the premises, yes, I can see the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this is a statement apparently taken on the 3rd but written up on the 4th. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now can we turn to tab 6, please, because this is a statement that you took. You see your signature on that, as well as the signature of your colleague, Mr. Jovovic, and the signature of Mr. Zenelj Alija. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And the opening words of that statement, do they say this: "As I failed to mention it in my previous statement on the 3rd of September ..." Are those the opening words? Could you read the opening words for us, please.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says there. Most likely this is in reference to the statement given previously by the public security members.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Precisely so. Now, I thought you gave evidence yesterday, and indeed repeated it today, Mr. Tomas, that you were not aware of the fact whether or not Mr. Alija had been interviewed by the MUP before you interviewed him. You told us that on oath this afternoon and on oath yesterday, and you gave evidence yesterday that you thought he'd been arrested on the day of your interview. Can you help us with that, please.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's precisely what I believe now. I didn't know that he had been arrested earlier. I believed that he was arrested on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, explain to us, please, how that answer makes sense, Mr. Tomas. We have here a reference in a statement that you have signed on the 11th of September referring to a previous statement dated the 3rd of September which, as you agreed a moment ago, is a statement taken by the MUP, which refers to the fact that Mr. Alija had been arrested on the 3rd of September. Now, would you agree that it's perfectly clear from the statement that we're looking at here that you have signed on the 11th of September that you must have seen and known about the statement that Mr. Alija is alleged to have given to the MUP on the 3rd of September because you refer to it?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was simply a participant in creating this document because I didn't speak the language. Most likely, since I didn't speak the language, I was there to help my colleague to create the document and to type it because I was a better typist. That's the only explanation I can give you. I typed down what was presented to me. That's the best explanation I can give you now. I can't interpret this in any other way. I didn't speak the language, so my role was reduced to helping create the document and type it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I understand this, please, Mr. Tomas. Is it your evidence that all the interviews then that you were present at were conducted in Albanian by your colleague?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, he interpreted the part of the interview he had back to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if you didn't speak the language, what was your function in the interview process itself? Why were you there?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something I said at the outset of my statement. I was assigned there to help my colleagues out. Where we were able to use the same language, I took an active participation in the activity; and in such cases as this one where I didn't know the language, I assisted my colleague and typed the document up.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So you typed this document, and you must have typed, therefore, those opening words: "As I failed to mention in my previous statement on the 3rd of September." They must be words that you typed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I most certainly typed that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You knew full well that he'd been interviewed by the MUP, didn't you, and that he'd been in detention since the 3rd of September?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN TOMAS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, what Mr. Emmerson puts to you is that if you typed out a statement in which someone corrects a statement he gave on the 3rd of September, at that moment you learn that that person has given a statement on the 3rd of September. Irrespective of what exactly your role was, but you typed that out as the statement of this person. And, therefore, Mr. Emmerson has difficulties in understanding how you could not have known about the statement on the 3rd, where you yourself typed out a later statement in which the person corrects his earlier statement. By the mere fact of typing it out, Mr. Emmerson has difficulties, as far as I understand, to have an explanation for your lack of knowledge of the earlier statement. Could you please comment on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to have knowledge of that statement, I would first have to see it. I suppose you'd agree with me. I did not have occasion to see the statement made by the members of the public security branch. I didn't see the statement. For me, everything started on the 7th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I think, as a matter of fact, that that may be correct and I think Mr. Emmerson is not saying that you were present during the 3rd of September, but Mr. Emmerson under those circumstances, I take it, would expect you to say: Well, I've not been present in any earlier interview. I was not aware of it on the 7th, but on the 11th of September, at least, the witness gave a statement in which he corrects an earlier statement. I've never seen, so I do not know whether it exists or not but at least that's what I learned about it. That's what, I think, Mr. Emmerson would have expected on the basis of your testimony on this typewritten document. And just to avoid whatever misunderstanding. If you have not seen that 3rd of September statement, but if you know something about it such as it being corrected at a later stage by the same witness, you are supposed to tell us. Do you have any other explanation for your testimony here where you said that you had no awareness of any earlier statement given by this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I repeat that I didn't know that. I didn't see the statement. As I said, we were merely handing these persons over to conduct interviews with them without receiving any documentation that had anything to do with them. So we didn't have any documents to begin with when we started these interviews, and it might have proved helpful to actually have the statements taken by the public security service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tomas, when you're asked whether you are aware of a previous statement given by a witness, that is not the same question as whether you had seen a document which -- in which the statement of the witness is written down. You should have told under those circumstances, if you would have remembered this, that although you had not seen it, that you typed out a statement in which this witness corrected an earlier statement taken before you got involved in the matter, that is, before the 7th of September. And may this be clear guidance for any future answer you give.
