In relation to the proposed testimony, it's no different to any other investigator, in any other Tribunal in the world, giving evidence as to the procedures of identification. It's the witness's identification. The investigator is called to describe the process of what the witness said. Whether the witness identified or recognised a person or did not is a matter to be assessed in the totality of the evidence. The witness should be called now. He's available to give his evidence, and it would very much would suit the convenience, in our respectful submission, for the Trial Chamber, the Defence, and the Prosecution to hear the evidence now and attribute the relevant weight at the appropriate point in the proceedings, and that's at the end of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I take full responsibility for asking at a relatively late time. And if it's the question of a plane ticket, I'm happy to pay for a plane ticket.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm saying that because I don't really think that is what the underlying issue is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I was about to say that the mere fact that the witness is here and costs have been paid is as such not full justification for calling the witness at this moment if there are other reasons why you --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you should refrain from calling him at this moment. The Chamber has considered the matter and the Chamber comes to the conclusion that there are no sufficient reasons at this moment to delay or postpone the testimony of the witness. Of course, the Chamber is aware that if at a later stage in view of what other witnesses would say if there would be any need - I'm not saying that there will be - but if there would be any pressing need to recall the witness, we will then consider it at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. I would like to turn my attention to the 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not going to dwell on the issue of when it was received, but rather address another problem which is the 92 ter statement, as it's presently constituted, summarizes statements made by witnesses. The inclusion of those matters are relevant to, as the Chamber just pointed out the reason by which this witness could be called -- the reason for which this witness could be called, the processes used to conduct the photo-board identifications. With regard to the statements of the witnesses themselves, that information must come from the witness himself in live testimony or appropriate written statements. It is a well-established belief -- rule of law here that it is improper for a prosecution investigator to present summaries of witness statements, and that was held in Milosevic case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes Mr. Guy-Smith, if I interrupt you, let's first try to seek clarification. Mr. Re, in the 92 ter statements, there are some summaries of what the witness stated. There are also some observations of Mr. Haverinen. Is it the summaries of what the witness stated is that context or do you intend that the Chamber should rely on those summaries in order to establish what the witness supposedly had said?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's mainly context. It may be -- it's up to the Defence. If there's a question they wish to question the investigator as to a difference between what a witness has allegedly said in a statement and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- in court, they can always do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's always possible, but it's not that if the Chamber would admit a 92 ter statement, where in the 92 ter statement we find summarized what will the witness said, that you expect the Chamber to consider this as a sufficient basis to establish that that's not only what the witness stated, but also that that is what we should adopt?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Might I attempt a formulation? I don't understand Mr. Re to be suggesting or the Trial Chamber to be ready to accept those passages of this 92 ter statement which contain summaries, as though it were tendered of evidence of the truth of its content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That being the case, then plainly, of course, any party might wish to cross-examine on inconsistencies, because that would not have been examining on what had been said in order to establish the truth of its content, but the inconsistency of what someone had said in the past. But providing it is clear that Mr. Re is not seeking, for example, in respect of Witness 30 when eliciting evidence about the manner in which a photo identification was conducted to go beyond that and to rely for the truth of its contents on this witness describing what Witness 30 said, the person he identified did, then in those circumstances --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That he identified perhaps a person on the photograph, but not then necessarily that we should adopt as the truth what the witness said about the person --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- may have done --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As far as I understand Mr. Re, in the light of the answer, is not suggesting that it's even tendered for that purpose; and on that basis, I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, is Mr. Emmerson right on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Not entirely. The descriptions by an investigator who has interviewed a witness is in the same category as any other hearsay evidence given in -- given before this Tribunal, which means that it could if the Tribunal wishes to use as corroboration of something someone else has said as the truth of the matter. That is primarily not why we are putting it there, but the it could be used like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think that's where I was going with regard to the specific issue that investigator's summaries of witness statements is improper under the Milosevic ruling of 30th of September, 2002, paragraphs 18 through 34. That cannot be done. That's simply just not the law. It cannot be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I may say so, if that is what Mr. Re is intending, then it gives rise to a fairly fundamental question of law which is going to need to be argued and perhaps be the subject of written submissions. Because if one takes Witness 30 as an example, let us assume that Witness 30 does not give evidence in these proceedings, the way in which Mr. Re has just addressed Your Honours would leave it open to the Prosecution to seek to rely upon what this witness says Witness 30 told him, as if it were any other form of hearsay evidence, and then therefore to tender it for the truth of its contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think, as a matter of fact, what Mr. Re seeks - but I don't know whether I'm right or not - is, for example, if other evidence will be led in relation to events on which the witness has given a statement, that the fact that a witness here identified a certain person and did give a statement, which is not -- I mean, if a witness would have given a statement saying something totally different, that would be an additional reason to have doubts on the other evidence; whereas, if a witness comes with the same story, then at least that statement is no specific reason to have doubts opt other evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's formulated in a negative way --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which is different from corroboration.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Plainly, there are circumstances in which a prior consistent statement is properly admissible to refute, for example, an allegation of recent fabrication. So, for example, if one puts to a

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's perfectly legitimate for the Prosecution to call an investigator to say, No, no, he hasn't; he told me that in 2004 and signed his witness statement to say that it. That's a different question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand, but I don't know whether that's true or not. Mr. Re just does not want to give up all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, with respect, I understand the desire to move on and deal with this pragmatically, but may I pose a simple hypothetical. Assume Witness 30 does not testify, paragraph 22 of the 92 ter statement describes a visual identification by photo-board of Mr. Haradinaj, and it goes on -- I mean, the paragraph could very well stop there, at the second sentence, but it goes on: "Witness 30 also stated that during his detention period in the KLA prison in Jablanica, he learned that Haradinaj was the main commander of the Dukagjin operational zone. He also stated he saw him visiting the HQ on a daily basis." Now, those two sentences are, in my submission, fundamentally objectionable if they are being tendered to show the truth of their contents. Were it were otherwise, there would be no point of us having a trial. Mr. Re could simply call the investigators who had taken on the witness statements and rely on the evidence as hearsay for the truth of its contents. And I think if we are going down that path - and I don't wish to be tendentious about it - but if we are going down that path, it requires some legal argument. I haven't understood, until Mr. Re said it, that that was what he was intending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I suggest the following. I'm looking at the clock. It seems that Mr. Re doesn't want to give away yet tiny little elements that he would consider not to be objected to at a later stage, although he doesn't know yet exactly what it is, but he just makes a reservation and say a clear no under no circumstances, whatever it may be, is not what he accepts. At the same time, it seems to me that the parties are not far away from each other. The Chamber would like the parties to see whether they can reach an agreement on a formulation on what the evidentiary value of this 92 ter statement could be and what it could not be. If the parties do not agree on the matter, then, of course, the Chamber will have to give a ruling; and then, of course, we have to make, again, a distinction between admission and evaluation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I was going to make a suggestion that what we do is, if we can't come to an agreement, that at least those areas that should be redacted in our view be made available to the Chamber, so that we can have a clear understanding of what the present concerns are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can't agree on the principle, you could still reach a very practical solution, for example, on the basis of the example just given by Mr. Emmerson. I would like to leave it to that. Mr. Emmerson, you said there was one issue. I'm hesitant to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Two seconds, it will take.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Literally. I'm going to apply for an extension of time for responding to the application to amend the indictment in respect of the counts and particulars concerning the death of Sanije Balaj. The trial in Kosovo to which a reference has been made has come to a conclusion with a verdict, but the judgement from that Trial Chamber is not yet available. And we would like, if we may, to be in a position to make representations to the Trial Chamber, once the judgement is available and we know the basis for which the individual concerned was conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, is there any objection against that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't object to an application for a reasonable extension of time. We don't know when the written judgement will be handed down. We made an application -- we've asked today for UNMIK to give us a copy - it was handed down orally - of the transcript, and we hope to have that will next week. And I'll also give that to the Defence as soon as I get it, and the Trial Chamber. A written judgement may take a lot longer. We have no idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, an open-ended extension of time will not be given. If you provide the Chamber relevant information, if you would like to, if you would explore the possibility of when.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I may say so, a transcript of the oral judgement may well assist. I raised it today because currently we are expected to respond tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. You are relieved from that duty for the time being, until you have filed this request for further time. Then, there's one matter, and it will not take me more than one minute. There were two witnesses subpoenaed for today. That is Witness 30, that's the witness I had in mind, as a matter of fact. But also another witness not enjoying protective measures at this moment, but one never knows what happens in the future, that is Witness 48 in the tentative order of testimony. Then another witness was subpoenaed to appear yesterday. The registry is invited to confirm whether any of these witnesses, and the witness for yesterday was the witness with pseudonym 10, appeared at the premises of the Tribunal and inform the Chamber about it. If there's no other matter, we'll adjourn until tomorrow, quarter past 2.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 27th day of June, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
